class.name: ShapeCast3DDirect
class.brief_description: A query for physics objects that uses a physics shape.
class.description: [admonition type="note" collapsible="true" open="false"] [b]Part of [i]Godot Engine: Conservatory Edition[/i].[/b] This is not available in the official build of Godot. [/admonition] This class provides a means to query the world for physics objects that collide with a specific shape.

method.name: cast
method.description: Perform a shape cast using the properties of this object as its settings, in the provided physics [param space]. Returns the amount of objects that were hit, to read from [member results].

method.name: cast_statically
method.description: Perform a shape cast without having to make a new instance of [ShapeCast3DDirect], using the provided [param parameters], in the provided physics [param space].

method.name: get_collision_mask_value
method.description: A convenience method for [member collision_mask] which allows reading a specific mask bit by index.

method.name: set_collision_mask_value
method.description: A convenience method for [member collision_mask] which allows setting a specific mask bit by index.

method.name: set_from_parameters
method.description: Updates the parameters of this cast instance to mimic those of the provided [param parameters].

members.member: If [code]true[/code], this shape cast can detect physics areas, typically created as [Area3D]s.
If [code]true[/code], this shape cast can detect physics bodies, typically created as [PhysicsBody3D]s.
The collision mask bits that represent the layers which can be hit.
This returns the collision-safe fraction from the first result. This is the highest percentage of [member motion] can be applied [i]without[/i] actually colliding with the object.
This returns the collision-unsafe fraction from the first result. This is the smallest percentage of [member motion] that can be applied in order to just barely, but consistently, cause a collision.

Set this to [code]true[/code] to change the filter list such that it is [b]inclusive[/b], that is, only objects in the list can be hit. Otherwise, it is [b]exclusive[/b], preventing those objects from being hit.
This is set to [code]true[/code] if the shape cast hit something.

The margin is a sort of brim added to this shape, which expands its surface outward. This makes collisions less accurate - the shape is effectively larger than it's supposed to be - but also makes them more consistent.
The velocity of the shape being casted. Note that if the shape will not be in motion, you should prefer [ShapeQuery3DDirect], which is simpler to compute but doesn't support moving shapes.
The maximum amount of collisions that will be acquired. If more than this many objects are detected by the shape, they will be skipped to avoid adding excessive computational load.
The amount of results that the last call to [method query] actually acquired.
The results of the last call to [method query].
The [RID] of the shape that this will use to query the world.
The transformation of this query in world space. Note that scaling is not advised as it often breaks most physics systems.
